html:
The Principality of Nitra was a Slavic state centred on the town of Nitra in western Slovakia in the early 800s. Its prince Pribina had the first known church in the region consecrated there around 828.

In 833 Mojmír I of Moravia drove Pribina out and joined Nitra to his lands, forming Great Moravia. Nitra kept its weight inside that state, and in 880 the pope made it the seat of a bishop. After the Magyar conquest it became a duchy inside the Kingdom of Hungary, often held by the king's heir. Slovaks today treat Nitra as the cradle of their history.
